subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should Codex computer durations intentionally stop honoring JavaScript-style hexadecimal, exponent, and fractional string coercions while continuing to accept finite JSON numbers and decimal integer strings?
rationale: The code and documented numeric-seconds contract support the narrowing, but only maintainers can confirm whether undocumented string forms have an upgrade-compatibility obligation.

options.title: Accept strict numeric grammar
options.body: Merge the current patch, keeping finite numeric fractions and decimal integer strings while treating other string forms as zero-duration input.

options.title: Preserve broader string compatibility
options.body: Revise the parser and tests to retain explicitly chosen string forms, with documentation defining their grammar and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Require JSON numbers only
options.body: Reject every string duration and document the stronger boundary, accepting a larger compatibility break for a simpler contract.

recommendation.title: Accept strict numeric grammar
recommendation.body: Merge the current patch, keeping finite numeric fractions and decimal integer strings while treating other string forms as zero-duration input.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work in the same Codex dynamic-tool timeout path makes this the best available owner for the compatibility decision.
